newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa industrials at new high after fx easing.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa industrials at new high after fx easing.

text.p: The easing of foreign exchange controls on South African individuals on Tuesday was welcomed by shares, lifting the industrial index to a new closing high despite a tumble in engineering firm Murray & Roberts.
But niggling worries that the move, which allows individuals a once-off 200,000 rand offshore investment, may weaken the rand boosted rand-hedge stock Richemont to a 1997 best.
Analysts described the relaxation, which forms part of government's phased removal of exchange controls, as a non-event and in line with authorities' expectations.

But dealers said caution was evident in the market and investors were seen adopting a wait-and-see attitude on Wednesday, eyeing the rand which earlier weakened over 1.5 cents although retracing back to overnight levels in late trade.
Dealers said stock gains on Tuesday were also helped by a rally on the bond and share futures markets, which were both pleased by the recovery in the rand.

The industrial index headed north, notching up its second consecutive closing high, to end up 18.2 points at 8,808.7. Gold shares overall added 3.6 points to 968.6, taking heart initially from the weaker rand and shrugging off bullion's fall to fresh 4 -1/4 year lows.
The all-share index was hardly moved at 7,420.1, a gain of 0.1 of a point.
